AdminLevel.description:
A level of lmgw's admin tools, written `off`, `read_only` or `full`:
what a device's admin tools may do now (the change feed's
`hello.self_admin` and `state.self_admin`), the level set on a device
key (`KeyRow.self_admin`, and `self_admin` in `key_create` and
`key_set`), or the gateway's own (`GatewayStatus.self_admin`,
`SettingsFull.self_admin`).

Forward compatible like every enum a client reads: a value a newer
gateway sends reads as [`AdminLevel::Unknown`], as sent, and writes back
unchanged. The document lists the known values only.

AgentBatchShape.description:
What a `batch` manifest can actually do, for the Run tab.

Derived server-side from the manifest **and the stored config**, because
both halves matter and only one of them is in the manifest: the review
columns are the author's, in the author's order, while the values an
editable field may be set to come from the config field `enum_from` names —
so widening the taxonomy is a config edit and the table picks it up.
A client re-deriving this from the manifest text would also lose the column
order, since a JSON object parses into a sorted map here.

apply_tools.description:
The tools Apply reaches, named next to the button so the reviewer knows
what is about to be called.

apply_tools_are_ceiling.description:
`apply_tools` is the ceiling the agent's token enforces rather than the
calls the step makes — true for a container, whose image decides. The
Run tab says "may call" instead of "calls".

columns.description: Review-table columns, in the manifest's order.

editable.description: Output fields the reviewer may override, with their allowed values.

has_apply.description: The manifest declares an apply step, so there is something to write.

has_classify.description: The manifest declares a per-item model call, so "Dry run" applies.

AgentBudget.description:
The visible bounds a turn runs under: one pair from Settings → Agents & tools,
never a second one invented per agent.

app.description:
This agent declares `run.service`, so it serves an app of its own — the card's
`app` chip, and a link to the App tab.

error.description:
Set when the stored manifest could not be read at all — a row written
by a newer build. The card still lists, saying why, rather than the
whole catalog failing.

kind.description: `chat` or `batch`.

labels.description: The tool labels this agent attaches, in manifest order.

model_alias.description:
The manifest's model alias, template and all — usually
`{{config.model}}`, in which case `effective_model` says what the
stored config resolves it to.

requires_ok.description: Every label resolves and every narrowed tool name is currently listed.

version.description: Free text from the manifest, informational.

warnings.description: Warnings that are not tool gaps.

AgentField.description:
One rendered config field. `ty` is `string | integer | number |
boolean | array`; `format` is `secret | model_alias | multiline | directory
| file` or empty.

access.description:
For a `directory` or `file` field: `ro` or `rw`, as the **manifest**
declared it. Empty for every other field — the mode is a
property of the agent, never of the form.

has_value.description:
For a `secret` field: whether one is stored. Always false otherwise —
the value itself is in `config`.

kind.description: `git`, `image` or `url`.

AgentPortability.description:
Whether the export of this agent lands on another box.

Shown before the download, never enforced: exporting to the same box is the
common case, and the wrong answer is a file that looks complete while naming
an image only the exporter has.

notes.description:
What the receiver would have to do, one sentence each. Empty when
`portable`.

portable.description: Nothing about this agent is local to this machine.

AgentProvenance.description:
Where this row's document came from.

`None` on the detail document for a row nobody installed from an image — an
agent written in the Definition editor has no package and says so by having
no provenance, rather than by carrying one full of empty strings.

`installed_at` and `pulled_at` are two facts on purpose: the first is when
the row was written from the image, the second when the digest was last
read. `agent_pull` moves only the second.

digest.description:
`podman image inspect --format '{{.Digest}}'` at the last read. Empty
when podman could not say — never a placeholder that reads like a digest.

image.description: The image reference as it was given at install, tag and all.

manifest_path.description: Where in the image the manifest was found (`/lmgw/agent.json`).

AgentRequirement.description:
One `tools[]` entry measured against what the gateway offers right now.

A gap is a warning, never a refusal: an agent is imported before its server
is wired, the same way a server is registered before its image is pulled.

install.description:
The manifest's install hint, for prefilling the MCP page. lmgw never
fetches anything from it.

missing_tools.description: Names in `allowed` the source does not list right now.

registered.description: The label resolves to a registered server or a built-in toolset.

AgentReviewField.description:
One editable output field. An empty `options` means free text: there is no
enum behind it to offer.

output.description: Any JSON value; carried into the stored result verbatim.

AgentRunEventsBody.description: One ledger event object ({row, ...} or {log: "..."} or {done: true, ...}) or a JSON array of them. The same events may be sent as application/x-ndjson instead, one object per line; lmgw reads the raw body either way, whatever its Content-Type. A line or entry it cannot parse is skipped and counted in the response's rejected list, and never fails the whole call.

AgentRunSummary.description:
One `agent_run` job as the Runs tab lists it.

The universal job fields plus the run's own `detail`/`result`, whose inner
shape belongs to the executor rather than to this DTO — the same
split `JobView` already makes for every other job kind.

cost_micro.description:
What those tokens cost, in micro-units of the gateway's currency.
`None` is "nobody could price this", which is also not zero.

duration_ms.description: Wall clock from claim to finish. `None` while it is still going.

model_calls.description:
The model calls the run made, from its result: calls answered without
an error. `None` until it has a result. `Some(0)` with no `cost_micro`
and no tokens is a run that had nothing to price; `Some(0)` can also
come with a cost, from calls that failed or were stopped after their
rows were priced.

tokens.description:
Prompt + completion tokens the run spent, from its result.
`None` until it has one — "not known yet", which is not zero.

AgentRuntime.description:
What a `container` agent runs under.

Every limit is here with its default printed next to it on the Run tab:
a container's bounds are shown, never guessed, like a run's tool-call and
wall-clock budget. `0` means "no
limit" everywhere except `stop_grace_seconds`, where it means SIGKILL at
once — the page says which.

output_validated.description:
The phases whose `output` event is validated against a declared schema.
A phase absent here is unvalidated, which the Run tab says out loud
rather than leaving the reader to assume a check that is not happening.

phases.description: Which phases the image implements, in declaration order.

podman_note.description: Why it did not, when it did not.

AgentService.description:
Service mode as the App tab describes it.

Everything a bound here is read from is a manifest field with its value
printed: the idle window, the start timeout and the health path are the
manifest's, and `0` means what it says everywhere else — never idle-stop,
and wait as long as the start takes.

health_path.description: `run.service.health_path`. Empty = a TCP connect instead of an HTTP GET.

host_port.description:
The host port this start published on — ephemeral, per start. `0` when
nothing is running.

idle_seconds.description: `0` = never idle-stop, exactly as an MCP server's `idle_seconds` means it.

idle_seconds_now.description:
How long ago the last proxied request finished. `None` when nothing is
running.

in_flight.description: Requests in flight, which is what the idle sweep skips on.

log_tail.description:
The container's own log tail, read while it is running. Empty when
nothing is up — `podman logs` on a container that is gone has nothing to
say.

log_tail_lines.description:
How many lines `log_tail` is at most, printed beside
it so nobody has to guess whether they are seeing all of it.

mounts.description:
The host mounts this agent's container holds, in the manifest's field order and
only the ones that are bound.

The App tab lists them. `host` is filled for an `Admin` reader and left
out for the container reading its own row, which is told
`/lmgw/mounts/<field>` and nothing else.

origin.description:
The origin this agent's UI is served on, as a URL with its slash:
`http://board.localhost:8001/`. The container's
own `LMGW_APP_ORIGIN` is the same origin *without* the slash — an
origin to concatenate onto, rather than an `href`.

origin_resolves.description:
`<id>.<suffix>` resolves on the machine lmgw is running on — the server
asked the resolver when it rendered this. False is not an error: the
App tab prints the `/etc/hosts` line that fixes it, and Chrome and
Firefox resolve `*.localhost` regardless of what the system says.

port.description: The in-container port the manifest declares.

provides_mcp.description:
`run.provides.mcp`, when declared: the path inside the container that
speaks MCP, registered as the `agent:<id>` server.

running.description: The container is up and answering.

start_timeout_seconds.description: `0` = wait as long as the container takes.

started_at.description: When the running container was started.

starting.description: A start is in flight right now.

AgentServiceMount.description: One bound mount as a reader is shown it.

field.description: The config field that names the slot.

host.description:
The canonical host path — **`Admin` only**. `None` is what the agent's
own view sees, and it is absent from the JSON rather than empty: a
container is not told there is a path it is not being given.

inside.description: `/lmgw/mounts/<field>` — what the container sees, for every reader.

kind.description: `directory` | `file`, from the field's `format`.

AgentToken.description: The agent's credential as the detail page describes it.

has_value.description:
A token has been minted. `false` until the first run or the first Copy
token: an agent that is never run never mints a credential.

name.description: `agent:<id>` — the name Logs and the usage page print.

scope_note.description:
The derived scope in words — "token: any model", or the aliases it is
fenced to. Shown next to Copy token so the scope is never invisible.

AgentWarning.description:
One warning that is not a tool gap.

Beside `requires`, of the same shape and rendered in the same place. The
Start gate is `requires_ok` **and** no warning with `blocks_start`.

AliasView.description: A model alias plus its resolved upstream name.

capabilities_override.description:
An alias's capabilities override for the derived `/v1/models` capability facts: a JSON
object with optional keys `capabilities`, `max_output_tokens`, `notes`. `None` = no
override.

content.description: A string, or an array of blocks: {type:text,text}, {type:image,source:{type:base64,media_type,data} | {type:url,url}}, {type:tool_use,id,name,input} (the id as lmgw gave it: a Gemini model's carries its thought signature and runs to hundreds of characters; echo it exactly, and do not send it to another provider directly), {type:tool_result,tool_use_id,content,is_error}, {type:thinking,thinking,signature} (replayed; unsigned when lmgw itself produced it), {type:redacted_thinking} (accepted and dropped: lmgw never asks an Anthropic upstream for thinking with a redaction key). A custom tool without input_schema (a server tool) is refused with 400.

system.description: A string, or an array of {type:text,text} blocks.

type.description: e.g. invalid_request_error, not_found_error, permission_error, overloaded_error, api_error.

items.description: {type:text,text} | {type:tool_use,id,name,input}; a leading {type:thinking,thinking} block when the completion carried reasoning (unsigned: produced by lmgw, not by Anthropic).

cache_creation_input_tokens.description: Present only when the upstream reported cache writes.

cache_read_input_tokens.description: Present only when the upstream reported a cache read.

content.description: A string, or an array of blocks: {type:text,text}, {type:image,source:{type:base64,media_type,data} | {type:url,url}}, {type:tool_use,id,name,input} (the id as lmgw gave it: a Gemini model's carries its thought signature and runs to hundreds of characters; echo it exactly, and do not send it to another provider directly), {type:tool_result,tool_use_id,content,is_error}, {type:thinking,thinking,signature} (replayed; unsigned when lmgw itself produced it), {type:redacted_thinking} (accepted and dropped: lmgw never asks an Anthropic upstream for thinking with a redaction key). A custom tool without input_schema (a server tool) is refused with 400.

output_config.description: lmgw reads output_config.effort as the same reasoning tier x-lmgw-reasoning-effort sets.

system.description: A string, or an array of {type:text,text} blocks, joined with blank lines.

thinking.description: {type:enabled,budget_tokens} | {type:disabled} | {type:adaptive} (enabled, no budget — "think as much as judged necessary").

tools.description: Custom tools only (input_schema required); a server tool (web_search, computer use, …) is refused with 400.

max_input_tokens.description: Alias of context_window, under the name the Anthropic SDK types it by.

prompt.description: USD per prompt token, as a decimal string; "0" for a local model.

AnthropicStreamEvent.description: SSE event: <type>, data: <this object>, one per line of the sequence above.

ApiError.description: Uniform error body for every non-2xx `/api` response.

message.description: Human-readable description, shown verbatim in the UI.

AppliedToCurrent.description:
What a folder patch applied to the folder's current thread (`applied`
in the patch's answer): the thread and the settings it changed, as the
thread settings name them (`temperature`, `voice.tts_alias`).

reason.description:
Why, for a declined call: the model reads "The user declined this
tool call: <reason>".

ApprovalRequest.description: One call that waits for an approval.

approval_request_id.description: The id a decision quotes (`mcpr_…`), unique in the gateway.

arguments.description: The arguments as the model wrote them: a JSON string.

call_id.description:
The call's id, as its `ready` and `result` frames carry it
([`crate::mcp_apps::ToolReadyFrame::call_id`]). Absent from an lmgw
before 2026-10-09, and from an [`ApprovalRequest`] read off a bound
session's `mcp_approval_request` item (OpenAI's shape has none):
there the `lmgw.chat.frame` relaying the `approval` frame has it.

name.description:
The tool's own name: the name the model called, without its
label's `<prefix>__`.

server_label.description: The thread's label the tool came from.

ArgList.description:
A list-valued argument as either surface sends it: newline/shell text from
the tool plane (every self-admin argument is a flat scalar) or a ready token
list from the dashboard, whose
editor already splits lines. Tokens are taken verbatim — re-parsing them
through shlex would eat the backslashes in an `--override-tensor` regex.

AttachmentFacts.description:
What extraction found in an attachment (`AttachmentMeta::meta`): which
keys are there depends on the kind. A key a gateway version adds is kept
beside these, so a reader never loses it.

format.description: An office file's or audio clip's format, as sniffed (`docx`, `wav`, ...).

parts.description: How many parts an office file has.

textless.description: A PDF's pages without a text layer, numbered from 1.

tokens.description:
The extracted text's token estimate (text, PDF, office files and
transcribed audio).

transcript_alias.description: The speech-to-text alias that wrote an audio clip's transcript.

transcript_error.description: Why an audio clip's transcription failed, until a retry succeeds.

AttachmentMeta.description: One attachment's metadata, never its bytes.

blockers.description: For a draft: why it cannot be sent to the thread's current model.

extracted_tokens.description: The extracted text's token estimate; `null` when there is none.

hints.description:
For a draft: what it becomes on the way, sent all the same (an image
as a placeholder, a PDF's pages as its text) under a fallback that
cannot see.

kind.description: `image`, `pdf`, `text`, `audio`, ... as the upload was classified.

meta.description:
What extraction found: pages, text-less pages, class, sheets,
transcript alias or error, tokens. `{}` for an image.

mode.description:
A text-class PDF's choice, `text` or `images`; `null` when it does
not apply or is not chosen yet.

AudioAlignmentsRequest.description: multipart/form-data only — lmgw's own route (for models whose row has task "align"), not an OpenAI shape.

AudioCatalogInstall.description:
`POST /api/op/audio_catalog` with `action: "download"` — the package's
files go through the shared HF download queue (target `audio`), exactly
like a wizard download.

ok.description: Always `true`.

revision.description:
The revision the files are fetched at: the commit the catalog pins
(under `audio.catalog_revision = pinned`), else `main`.

AudioCatalogRefreshed.description: `audio_catalog` with `action: refresh`: the catalog was fetched anew.

families.description: How many model families the catalog holds.

ok.description: Always `true`; a warning does not fail a refresh.

warnings.description:
What the refresh could not do (a spec file that did not load, a
package repository Hugging Face could not list).

any_installed.description: At least one package fully downloaded.

builtin_voices.description:
Voices the family ships, and which it uses by default — enough to
configure a TTS row before its container has ever run.

capabilities.description: Per-task capability tags, as the spec writes them.

category.description: Free-form spec category (`tts`, `asr`, …) — a badge, not an enum.

docs.description: `ui.docs` — paths into the audio.cpp repo, rendered as links.

options.description: The typed options this family accepts, by group.

served.description:
An enabled audio model of this family loads one of its packages
(some package's `served`). A row that points at the family's files
without saying which package is the packages' `serving_unclear`; one
that loads nothing of the family is `serving_note`.

serving_note.description:
One sentence per enabled row of this family that matches none of its
packages — an empty or missing root, a `weight_id` that picks no file,
GGUFs no package ships — joined by "; ". Empty when there is none.

status.description:
`supported` | `community` | `experimental` | `testing` | `wip` — how
finished upstream calls this family. Empty when the spec is older than
the field.

summary.description: One extra line the spec offers beside the description.

tags.description: `ui.tags` — short labels from the project's own WebUI.

AudioFamilyOption.description: One declared option: name, type, and whatever bounds the spec states.

default.description: The engine's default, as JSON; absent when the spec states none.

kind.description:
`string` | `int` | `float` | `bool` | `enum` | `path` | … — the spec's
own vocabulary, not an enum on this side of the wire.

values.description: Accepted values of an enum option (a named preset already expanded).

AudioFamilyOptions.description:
A family's declared options, split the way they are configured: `load` and
`session` are the two JSON objects on the model row, `request` is what a
call may carry.

anyOf.description: The chat model reads the transcript.

A chat model that takes audio hears the turn; the transcript is
made beside it.

AudioInputMode.description: Whether a voice turn may reach the chat model as audio.

AudioLabModel.description: One enabled audio model, as the lab's pickers need it.

alias.description: The alias to send as `model`: the audio prefix and the model id.

family.description: The engine family the model runs in (audio.cpp's own name for it).

mode.description: `offline` or `streaming`; only a streaming model can stream speech.

task.description:
What the model does: `tts`, `asr`, `align` or another audio.cpp task.
Decides which panel the lab offers.

AudioLabUploadRequest.description: multipart/form-data. The body size is not limited.

file.description: A clip; send as many file parts as there are clips. A part's file name names the clip: letters, digits, space, '.', '_' and '-', not starting with '.' (anything else is a 400). A clip with the name of a stored one replaces it.

transcript.description: What the clip says. Applied only when the upload holds exactly one file; blank is ignored.

AudioModel.description: An audio model row (JSON-map fields stay dynamic).

backend.description:
`cpu` runs this row on the CPU (no VRAM, served under the GPU hold);
`None` inherits the class's backend.

busy_timeout_ms.description:
Per-model `busy_timeout_ms` and the ceiling a request's own value is
clamped to, in ms; `None` inherits the class.

config_id.description: Named config/weights asset ids, for a model directory holding several.

default_request_options.description: Request-option defaults applied to every call to this model.

extra_run_args.description:
Per-model `podman run` args override; `None` inherits the audio
class settings' `extra_run_args`.

hold_fallback.description:
The alias to route to while the GPU is held, meaningful only when
`hold_fallback_mode` is `alias`.

hold_fallback_mode.description:
GPU-hold fallback mode: `inherit` | `none` |
`alias`. `inherit` means "no fallback" for this class — audio models
never inherit the global chat alias.

image.description:
Per-model container image override;
`None` inherits the audio class settings' image.

lazy.description: Per-model override of the class's `lazy_load`; `None` inherits.

model_spec_override.description:
A `<family>.json` model spec (or a directory of them) under the audio models
dir that replaces the container image's own catalog for this row.

residency.description:
What this model's container was measured to hold on the GPU once it
had served a request. Learned by the gateway,
never by the editor; `audio_model_set`'s `clear: "residency"` resets
it. `None` = not learned, charged at the on-disk size.

threads.description:
Per-row thread count; `None` inherits (this machine's physical cores
for a row switched to the CPU itself, else the class's — for a row
that inherits a class backend of `cpu` too).

warm_start.description: Start this model's own container at app launch.

backend.description: `cpu` when the row is switched to the CPU; null inherits the class.

effective_extra_run_args.description: The `podman run` args in effect, one per line.

effective_image.description: The image the container starts from (the row's, else the class's).

extra_run_args.description: `podman run` args override, one per line; null inherits.

image.description: Container image override; null inherits the audio class's.

next_step.description: How to prove the model works.

path.description: The model directory, relative to the audio models dir.

public_name.description: The name clients call it by, with the audio prefix.

residency.description: What the container was measured to hold on the GPU.

residency_charged_bytes.description:
The learned residency admission charges, when it belongs to the
current configuration.

residency_note.description: What the row is charged on the GPU, in a sentence.

running.description: The container's state, when one is running.

server_json.description: The `server.json` entry this row renders to.

residency_charged_bytes.description:
The learned residency admission charges this row: `model.residency`'s
figure while it belongs to the row's current configuration, `None`
otherwise (not learned, or learned for a previous configuration — the
on-disk size is charged then).

residency_note.description:
What the row is charged on the GPU and why, in one sentence: its learned residency, or the
on-disk size it is charged
at instead — not learned yet, learned for a previous configuration, or
not learnable on this host (and why).

runs_on.description:
Where the row runs as configured now: `gpu` | `cpu` (its own
`backend`, else the class's). A running container keeps the placement
it was started with until it stops.

threads_source.description:
Where that count comes from: `row` | `class` | `cores` (this
machine's physical cores, for a row switched to the CPU that names
none) | `logical_cpus` (the same, where the core topology could not
be read and the figure is the logical CPU count).

AudioPackage.description:
One installable package (a file set of a family) plus everything the UI
needs to show its state and to prefill the audio-model editor from it.

availability_note.description:
What is known about whether the repo publishes this package's files,
when it is not simply "all of them": the missing ones with the date of
the listing, or why the repo could not be listed. Empty otherwise.

description.description: What this package is, when the spec says so (a size, a trade).

download_ids.description:
Tracked download rows for this package's files — the UI joins them
against `GET /api/hf/downloads` for live progress.

downloaded_from.description:
Which commit the downloaded files came from, as a sentence — the
commit and the revision the download asked for, or "unknown" for files
downloaded before lmgw recorded it. Empty when nothing is downloaded.

gated.description:
The repo needs an accepted licence and a token: downloading it without
one fails with 401s, so the UI says so before the click.

incomplete.description:
Downloaded once and short of `missing_files` now, with nothing on
its way: a download ("complete install") fetches those — and, while
a pin is followed, the package's installed files from another commit
than the pin, so the package is one commit again.

installed.description: Every file downloaded — the package can be served.

missing_files.description:
Spec files the package lacks on this machine, once any of it was
downloaded: no finished download, or the file is gone from disk. A
spec that grew after the package was installed (a new built-in
voice) shows up here.

pin_followed.description:
Whether a download takes `pinned_commit`: true under
`audio.catalog_revision = pinned`, false under `latest`, which takes
`main` even though the spec pins one. False when nothing is pinned.

pinned_commit.description:
The commit the spec pins the package to — its `revision` when that is
a full commit hash; empty when it pins none.

precision.description: `q8_0`, `f16`, … — empty when the spec names none.

recommended.description: audio.cpp's recommended package for the family.

repo.description:
Hugging Face repo the files come from; empty = no download source in
the spec, so the package cannot be installed from here.

revision.description:
The revision the spec names for the package's repo (`main`, or a
commit), as written; empty when it names none.

served.description:
An enabled audio model loads this package's weights: the weights file
lmgw takes the row to load (the GGUFs under its root, narrowed by its
`weight_id`) belongs to this package and no other — or, for a package
without GGUFs, the package is downloaded and the only one under the
row's root. Implies the weights are on disk.

served_by.description: The `model_id`s of the rows that serve it.

serving_unclear.description:
Non-empty when a row points at this package's files without telling
it apart from another package (its root holds several and no
`weight_id` picks one): what it is and how to settle it, one sentence
per such row.

size.description: Human size of the downloaded files, empty until they are on disk.

unavailable_reason.description:
Why this package cannot be installed from here, in upstream's words —
a licence that forbids redistribution, a GGUF build not published yet.
Empty when it can.

unpublished_files.description:
Spec files the repo does not publish, as of the refresh that listed
it at the revision a download takes (the pin, when followed): the spec
is ahead of the weights, and a download would be refused.

AudioSettings.description:
The audio class settings: the same fields as the chat/aux class settings,
plus the engine fields that flow into every audio model's own
`server.json`.

busy_timeout_ms.description:
How long a request waits for a model that is already running before it
fails with `503 server_busy`, in ms. **0 = wait forever.**

catalog_revision.description:
What an audio catalog download takes: `pinned` (the commit the spec
pins, `main` where it pins none — the default) or `latest` (`main`).

idle_unload_ms.description:
Unload the resident model after this long without a load or run,
freeing its VRAM while the container stays up. **0 = never.**

max_request_body_mb.description:
Largest request body audiocpp_server buffers, in MiB. **0 = leave the
key out**, so the engine's own 2 GiB default applies.

min_free_memory_mb.description:
Free memory (host and GPU) a model load must leave behind, in MiB.
**0 = no guard.**

request_timeout_seconds.description:
Per-request ceiling for the class, in seconds. 0 = the maximum possible — no deadline of
lmgw's own.

voice_dir.description:
Shared voice library as the container sees it (`/models/voices` by
default — the Audio lab's own clips). Empty = no library.

voice_transcribe_alias.description:
The speech-to-text model that writes voice-library clip transcripts
(its configured fallback answers as for any request). Empty = none:
nothing is transcribed automatically.

catalog_revision.description:
`pinned` | `latest`. Set by the save, not by `apply`: it is not part
of the class's container definition.

voice_transcribe_alias.description: Checked by the save (a local `asr` row, or empty), not by `apply`.

AudioSpeechRequest.description: OpenAI's TTS shape plus audio.cpp's own request options, forwarded with model rewritten to the upstream's own id; a row's configured voice presets apply on top. input may carry inline tags ([laughs], or a stage direction such as (sighs)): rendered by a model whose capabilities.speech.inline_tags says so, stripped everywhere else — never read out. An input of nothing but tags is 400 empty_input, refused before any model is started.

input.description: The text. A local model whose engine refuses a character its package lacks (Supertonic) is sent an equivalent it has in its place, or nothing; the x-lmgw-speech response header names each one. An input left with nothing to say (a lone emoji) is 400 empty_input, refused before any model is started.

instructions.description: A speaking style, or the description a voice-design model builds its voice from (required there: 400 instructions_required without one, unless the row has a default). Dropped for a model that reads none: capabilities.speech.instructions says which, and the x-lmgw-speech response header says when.

language.description: An ISO 639-1 code or BCP-47 tag; a local model gets it in its own vocabulary.

stream_format.description: Streams PCM16 (with response_format pcm) as speech.audio.delta events (sse) or as raw chunked PCM (audio). A local model streams only when its row runs in streaming mode; an offline row is 400 streaming_unsupported before anything starts (capabilities.speech.streaming says which). The x-lmgw-sample-rate response header states the PCM's rate.

voice.description: A row's own voice preset id, when it defines any (GET /v1/audio/voices). A voice-library clip with no transcript, for a model that cannot clone one without, is 400 voice_needs_transcript before anything starts (lmgw.needs_transcript in the voice list); send reference_text, or transcribe the clip in the dashboard's Audio lab. A local model whose audio.cpp image lacks eSpeak NG is 400 audio_image_lacks_espeak.

AudioTranscriptionDetails.description: The same transcription, plus the detail arrays the plain route leaves out.

AudioTranscriptionsRequest.description: multipart/form-data (also accepted as application/json with the same fields but no upload: instead of file, audio names a clip by its path on the model server's own filesystem, e.g. /models/clip.wav, and the body is relayed with model rewritten; the multipart form is what real clients send).

AudioVoices.description: lmgw's own route. A local audio model is answered from lmgw's catalog without starting it (?probe=engine asks its own server, starting it); a remote one is asked.

lmgw.description: Only on a local audio model answered from lmgw's catalog (x-lmgw-voices-source: config).

default.description: What speaks when a request names no voice.

send.description: Where lmgw puts the name in the engine's request; clients always send it as `voice`.

transcript.description: A library clip's transcript is recorded.

held.description: The GPU hold (or a benchmark run) holds the card and the model has no fallback: the list stands, its speech is refused (503 gpu_hold) until the hold is released.

missing.description: Voices the spec names whose file the package lacks.

needs_transcript.description: The model cannot clone a library clip without its transcript: speech with an entry whose `transcript` is false is refused (400 voice_needs_transcript) until it has one (the dashboard's Audio lab, Transcribe).

voices.description: Every name the model answers to as `voice`, sorted; for a probe of the engine or of a remote upstream, as that source sent it.

AuxModel.description: An aux container model row — embedders and rerankers alike.

extra_run_args.description:
Per-model `podman run` args override; `None` inherits the aux
class settings' `extra_run_args`.

hold_fallback.description:
The alias to route to while the GPU is held, meaningful only when
`hold_fallback_mode` is `alias`.

hold_fallback_mode.description:
GPU-hold fallback mode: `inherit` | `none` |
`alias`. `inherit` means "no fallback" for this class — aux models
never inherit the global chat alias.

image.description:
Per-model container image override;
`None` inherits the aux class settings' image.

kind.description: `embed` | `rerank`.

warm_start.description: Start this model's own container at app launch.

AuxModelDetail.description: An aux (embedding or rerank) model read back.

command_line.description: The `podman run …` command line this model renders to.

endpoint.description: The route that serves it: `/v1/embeddings` or `/v1/rerank`.

extra_run_args.description: `podman run` args override, one per line; null inherits.

image.description: Container image override; null inherits the aux class's.

kind.description: `embed` or `rerank`.

problems.description: Static findings; empty is not proof it loads.

public_name.description: The name clients call it by, with the aux prefix.

run_id.description: The running run, for the `run_going` reason.

BenchComparison.description: A run against another: the previous comparable run for `bench_run`.

comparable.description: Same model file, settings hash, suite version and GPU.

regressions.description:
Metrics and probes flagged each way (`not_same_point` and
`missing` count for neither).

BenchOverrides.description:
What a run changes about the row's container, and only about the
bench container. `None` (and `false`, `0`) is "as the row says".

image.description:
Another image, e.g. a Backends build (comparing two builds is two runs
of one row with two images).

no_draft.description: Run without the row's speculative drafter.

BenchRun.description: One stored run, whole: every column, the JSON ones typed.

status_reason.description:
Why it ended the way it did, in one word where there is one
(`hold`, `canceled`, `shutdown`).

unreadable.description:
The JSON columns that did not decode, each as "<column>: <why>". Each reads as its empty
default here, so the run
is comparable with nothing ):
read as empty, it would compare as "measured nothing".

BenchRunSummary.description: One row of the runs table.

complete.description: Every selected phase finished without an error.

engine_slug.description:
`dev.lmgw.slug`, `org.opencontainers.image.version`, the commit and
`/props` `build_info` — whichever the build has.

previous_id.description: The previous comparable run, when there is one.

probes_passed.description:
Probes that passed, and probes that gave a verdict (`pass`, `fail`,
`error` — not `info` or `skipped`).

unreadable.description:
The stored columns that did not decode. Such a
run is listed with what could be read, and compared with nothing.

BenchSettings.description:
The `settings` of a run: what the bench container runs,
after the overrides.

**The settings hash covers `params`, `args` and `extra_run_args` only**: the image is the build
identity and may differ between
comparable runs (that is the point of comparing builds), the weights file
is the model identity, and `overrides` only says how these values came
about — the same effective flags reached with or without an override are
the same settings.

args.description:
The row's freeform llama-server flags (minus the drafter's, with
`no_draft`).

extra_run_args.description: `podman run` flags (GPU devices, …): the row's, or its class's.

gguf_path.description:
The weights file, relative to the chat models dir (the rung's own for
a ladder rung).

image.description: The resolved image the run starts (override, row, or class default).

params.description: The effective `LlamaParams`, as the row stores them.

oneOf.description:
Ended by something other than a cancel request — the GPU hold
switching on (`status_reason: "hold"`).
Found `running` at boot: lmgw went away mid-run.

BenchStop.description: One container a start stops — what the confirmation lists.

busy.description:
Serving lmgw requests right now, or still starting: the run waits for
it to drain rather than cutting it off. A client generating on the
container's own port is only seen at start time (`/slots`).

BlockedReason.description: Why a run cannot start now.

oneOf.description: The GPU hold is on: a benchmark is lmgw using VRAM.
Another run holds the card; `run_id` names it.
No chat row has this id.
The id names an aux, audio or image row.
`rung` is past the row's top rung.

The image is not on this machine: `podman run` would pull it and the
load phase would time the download.
The chat models dir is not configured, or the weights are not in it.

lmgw has just started and has not yet adopted the containers a
previous lmgw left running: the drain could not see them yet.

The `image` override is not an image reference: it starts with `-`
(podman would read it as a flag) or holds whitespace.

arch.description:

cuda_version.description: `None` = the preset's default for the engine.

dockerfile.description: Repo-relative Dockerfile path. `None` = the preset's candidates.

edits.description:
`None` = the preset's edits for the resolved Dockerfile; `Some` = this

extras.description: Merged on top of `git_ref`, in order.

keep_layers.description:

keep_runs.description: How many previous runs' immutable tags to keep. `None` = keep all.

ref.description: Branch, tag or commit to build on.

repo_url.description:

slug.description:
Becomes the tag. Tag charset, bounded so the longest immutable tag

BuildEdit.description:
One Dockerfile edit: a literal find/replace of
**every** occurrence, applied to a copy of the Dockerfile, never to the
checkout, in list order (a later edit sees what the earlier ones wrote).
Each one is logged as applied or not matched; a `required` edit that does
not match fails the run.

`find` and `replace` may carry `{{ccache_id}}`, `{{npm_cache_id}}`,
`{{ccache_max_size}}`, `{{ccache_shared_mount}}`/`{{ccache_seed}}` and
`{{npm_shared_mount}}`/`{{npm_seed}}`, filled in per run, so an edit list
stays the same when only a cache id or the size changes. The last two
pairs render empty for a plain build; with extras they mount the shared
ccache/npm cache read-only and seed the build's own from it. `name` and
`role` are for the log and the ccache switch; neither changes the image,
so neither is hashed.

name.description: Short label for the log and the editor (`ccache-mount`). May be empty.

One entry of a build's ordered extras list: something merged on top

With no `pin`, a run follows the head. A pin is a full commit SHA and

oneOf.description: A PR (GitHub) or MR (GitLab) of the build's own `repo_url`.

The build the run measured, filled in by the benchmark runner from the image and its labels,

job_id.description:
The background job that executed it (`JobKind::BuildRun`). Not a

promoted.description:
lmgw last moved the build's moving tag to this run's image. At most
one run per build carries it. podman is the source of truth: a tag

slug.description:
Snapshot of the build's slug and engine, so a run stays readable after

tags.description:
Every tag this run put on its image (immutable, and the moving tag

verify.description: The verify checks' results, shaped by the executor.

BuildRunInputs.description: A run's `inputs` column: the full snapshot.

cfg_hash.description:
Full sha256 hex of the image-affecting inputs; the immutable tag
carries its first 6 characters. `None` until resolved.

config.description:
The build definition exactly as it was when the run started — a run
outlives edits to its build, and the build itself.

resolved.description: `None` until the run has resolved its refs (phase 1).

oneOf.description:
Still going — including waiting for the machine-wide build lock, which

Not promoted; **Verify now** can finish the job later.
Built, and a verify check failed. Not promoted.
Did not produce an image.

The immutable tag for these exact inputs already existed and was
verified; nothing was built.

CandidateAliasView.description:
A candidate alias: its stored fields plus what lmgw computes from the live snapshot
(never stored, recomputed on every read).

advisories.description:
A candidate with `--cache-ram 0`: not an error, but worth
flagging.

candidates.description:
Local chat model ids, first = primary, rest = alternates in
preference order.

capabilities_disabled.description: The explicit "turn this common facet off" list (wire facet names).

common_facets.description:
Facets every candidate currently supports — the ceiling a save may
enable.

context_length.description:
Minimum across `routable` (a ladder candidate at its top rung);
absent if any of them is unknown or nothing is routable.

deferrals_24h.description:
How many `gpu_deferred` refusals this alias logged in the last 24
hours. `Some(0)` is a real
zero; `None` only ever means a frame cached from before this field
existed (`#[serde(default)]`), never "unknown".

enabled_facets.description:
The stored enabled facet set (`capabilities_enabled` as last saved —
see that field's own doc comment for why this is never recomputed
outside a save).

fallback_usable.description:
The alias fallback resolves, is not local, and supports every enabled
facet.

problems.description: What is wrong with a candidate or the fallback, in prose.

routable.description: Candidates the gate may actually route to right now, in list order.

unsupported_by.description:
Facet wire name -> candidate ids that do not support it (the editor's
"not supported by: <ids>").

head_id.description: What a client passes as `previous_response_id` to continue.

completion_tokens_details.description: Present only when the upstream reported reasoning tokens.

prompt_tokens_details.description: Present only when the upstream reported prompt-cache counts, and each field only when reported: cached_tokens read from the cache, cache_write_tokens written to it. Both are part of prompt_tokens.

ChatCompletionChunk.description: One frame: `data: <this object>`, repeated, ending with the literal `data: [DONE]`.

usage.description: Only with stream_options.include_usage: null on every frame but the last, whose choices is [] and which carries the request's usage.

completion_tokens_details.description: Present only when the upstream reported reasoning tokens.

prompt_tokens_details.description: Present only when the upstream reported prompt-cache counts, and each field only when reported: cached_tokens read from the cache, cache_write_tokens written to it. Both are part of prompt_tokens.

chat_template_kwargs.description: Only enable_thinking is read (llama-server's own template toggle, distinct from the protocol-neutral reasoning controls above); every key is forwarded verbatim.

max_completion_tokens.description: Wins over max_tokens when both are sent.

content.description: A string, or an array of parts: {type:text,text}, {type:image_url,image_url:{url}} (a plain URL or a data: URI), {type:input_audio,input_audio:{data,format}} (data: URI, or raw base64 with format required). A tool message keeps only its text, as OpenAI defines it; any other part is dropped with a WARN naming it.

name.description: role: tool only. Forwarded as the tool result's name.

reasoning_content.description: role: assistant only. Replayed as the leading reasoning part (also accepted spelled 'reasoning', as OpenRouter spells it; DeepSeek and llama.cpp use reasoning_content).

role.description: system and developer are both treated as a system message; tool and function are both treated as a tool-result message.

tool_calls.description: role: assistant only: [{id, type:function, function:{name, arguments: <JSON string>}}]. Send each id back as lmgw gave it: a Gemini model's call id carries the model's thought signature, which Gemini 3 refuses a replayed call without. Such ids run to hundreds of characters; echo them exactly, and do not send them to another provider directly (lmgw strips the signature there).

model.description: An alias, a local model id, a candidate alias, or 'prefix/…' to pass through to an exposed upstream.

reasoning.description: lmgw extension, OpenRouter's shape: {effort, max_tokens, enabled, exclude}. Read for the reasoning tier and forwarded verbatim.

reasoning_budget_tokens.description: lmgw extension: a thinking-token budget (also x-lmgw-reasoning-budget). Forwarded verbatim alongside thinking_budget_tokens — whichever spelling a llama-server version reads.

reasoning_effort.description: lmgw extension: an effort level, or 'none' for off — one spelling of the reasoning control (also x-lmgw-reasoning-effort, and reasoning.effort below); the header wins when both are sent.

stop.description: A string, or an array of strings.

stream_options.description: With stream: true, include_usage ends the stream with a chunk whose choices is [] and that carries usage; every other chunk then has usage: null. Without it no chunk carries usage. Not forwarded: lmgw asks the upstream for usage itself, for its request log.

thinking_budget_tokens.description: Same as reasoning_budget_tokens; both are read and both stay in the forwarded body.

top_k.description: Not part of the OpenAI API, but accepted; llama.cpp supports it.

ChatCompletionStreamError.description: The frame a stream carries instead of a chunk when the upstream fails after the first byte was sent.

ChatTestPassed.description:
A chat model that loaded and answered, with the comparison of its running
build against the gateway's static derivation.

class.description:
`aux` for an aux model's pass, `chat` where this is the first part of
a chat model's.

disagreements.description:
Where the running build and the static derivation disagree; empty
when they agree or `/props` could not be read.

latency_ms.description: How long the load and the probe took, in milliseconds.

note.description: Why `props` could not be read, when it could not.

ok.description: Always `true`.

props.description:
llama-server's own `/props` answer, verbatim; null when it could not
be read.

scored.description: For `rerank`: how many documents came back scored.

static.description:
The capabilities the gateway derived statically, the part `/props`
also states an opinion on.

CheckMergeStep.description: One extra's row in a `build_check_merge` report.

files.description: Conflicted paths — set only when `outcome` is `conflict`.

rendered as such — never as markdown, since it carries its own fences.

ChunkSpan.description: Where a chunk sits in its file, without its text.

page.description: 1-based page, slide or sheet, when the file has them.

seq.description: The chunk's position in the file.

span_start.description: Byte range in the file's extracted text.

30,000".

reason.description: Why — the numbers of the request that did not fit.

seconds.description: Since the mark, in whole seconds.

stage.description: What it is doing right now, in words.

name.description: The file name, extension included.

server_path.description:

voice.description:

by.description: Who wrote it, in a sentence.

transcript_source.description:

n_predict.description: llama.cpp spelling of max_tokens; folded into it for local models with a guard or a ladder.

prompt.description: A string, an array of strings, an array of token ids, or a mix of both.

aggregate_tok_s.description: Σ `predicted_n` / (last stream's end − first stream's first token).

energy.description: Over the aggregate's window; tokens are Σ `predicted_n`.

energy_unmeasured.description:
Why `energy` is `None` although the card reports power: a window
shorter than the GPU sampler resolves (two of its ticks, 200 ms at
the 100 ms tick), whose figure would have been the
ticks' average power times its length rather than a measurement.
`None` otherwise.

per_stream_tok_s.description: The median of the streams' `predicted_per_second`, per repetition.

ContainerAdvisories.description: A model that starts but misbehaves under some input.

ContainerBusy.description: A model whose container is still serving requests.

in_flight.description: How many requests it is serving.

ContainerFailure.description: A model an action failed on.

ContainerImage.description: One local or external image of the three engines.

backend.description:
The `dev.lmgw.backend` label, when present — a free string because
an external image (a `build.sh` tag, a registry pull) may not carry
it at all.

engine.description: `None` when the image can't be matched to an engine.

external.description: No `dev.lmgw.run` label — a `build.sh` image or a registry pull.

provenance.description: `None` for an external image lmgw did not build.

registry_update.description:
The registry update check for an image a class
default or model override uses under a registry name (not
`localhost/`). `None` for every other image, and before the first
check.

run_status.description: The run this image came from, when it is one lmgw built.

ContainerModel.description: A model named by class and id.

ContainerPort.description: A model and the port its container is up on.

port.description: The loopback port the container is published on.

ContainerProblems.description: A model with problems found by the static checks.

ContextExcerpt.description: One retrieved excerpt, as a user message stores it.

file.description: The file's name when it was retrieved.

file_sha.description:
The sha256 of the file version the chunk was cut from; empty for a
context stored before it was kept.

kb.description: The base's name when it was retrieved.

span_start.description: Byte range in the file's extracted text.

ContinueState.description: Whether a thread's last reply can be continued, and why not.

fence.description: Domains a fetch may touch; empty = the root's own host.

kind.description: `llms_txt | markdown | rustdoc_json | html`.

CorpusStatusView.description: The corpus status badges (embedding and evaluation state). Neither blocks a query.

embed_model_resolvable.description:
Whether a model on this gateway still resolves to the corpus's pinned
embedding identity. `false` with `embed_status` `re_embed_required`
means the corpus cannot be queried until it is re-embedded; `true`
means it is mid re-embed and still answers.

CorpusView.description: One corpus as the list and the detail view both show it.

embed_identity.description: `upstream/model@dims`, the pinned identity in one string.

eval_score.description: Latest measured hit@k; absent = never evaluated, which is not zero.

flags.description: Machine-readable badges; `warnings` is one sentence per flag.

resident_bytes.description:
What serving this corpus costs once resident: the visible price of
the exact-KNN scan.

unembedded_chunks.description:
Chunks with no vector yet; non-zero means the KNN stage sees only part
of the corpus.

CountTokensRequest.description: Routed by model exactly like the chat endpoints, so counting a cold local model's tokens starts its container. The key's alias scope applies: a refused count answers 403 key_scope and is logged; a successful count is not logged. No budget applies, neither the key's nor the gateway's: a count costs nothing.

CurrentReason.description: Why `current` answered with a new thread.

oneOf.description:
The folder had no current thread (for a device key: none it can
reach).

Its current thread can no longer be continued in the folder. Only
the dashboard and admin keys are given this reason.
Its current thread had no message for the folder's idle minutes.
The caller asked for a new thread (`new: true`).

depth.description: *D*: the prompt length the generation starts from.

distinct_token_ratio.description:
Distinct token ids over generated ones, per repetition: near 1 for
prose, low for a degenerate loop that `ignore_eos` ran into — and a
loop is what a drafter predicts perfectly, so a draft acceptance
next to a low ratio flatters it. Only where the
engine streams token ids (official llama.cpp, not ik).

energy.description:
Over first token → last token of each repetition, so the priming
prefill stays out; tokens are those generated after the first.

energy_unmeasured.description:
Why `energy` is `None` although the card reports power: a window
shorter than the GPU sampler resolves (two of its ticks, 200 ms at
the 100 ms tick), whose figure would have been the
ticks' average power times its length rather than a measurement.
`None` otherwise.

evaluated_tokens.description:
`timings.prompt_n`: the first repetition primes the cache (≈ *D*), the
later ones reuse it (a handful).

DictatedVoice.description:
How a dictated message says it was dictated (`voice` of a send): the
facts of the transcribe answer, nothing a reply carries. Unknown fields
are refused.

asr.description: The speech-to-text alias that was asked.

asr_answered_by.description: The alias that answered in its place, when a fallback did.

via.description:
Must be `dictation`: a realtime turn is written by the bound session
and cannot be sent.

DiskInfo.description:
`container_images`' `disk` field:
`podman system df` totals plus orphaned build leftovers, shown for
information only — nothing is pruned from here.

buildah_orphans.description:
`/var/tmp/buildahNNN` dirs and `Storage` containers not yet cleaned
up.

client_name.description: MCP client name from `initialize`, when it gave one.

version.description: Empty when the requester pinned no version.

DocsSearchDefaults.description:
The stage defaults (`Settings.docs_search`) — where a request that
overrides nothing starts. None of these is a cap: every one is a
per-request parameter the playground and `docs__query` can override.

budget_tokens.description: `0` means *no budget* — every one of `limit` chunks comes back.

eval_k.description: Depth an eval run measures hit@k at when the request names no `k`.

fts_weights.description:
BM25 column weights — a stage default like any other, and one the
playground exposes, so it has to round-trip through a save.

DocsSearchPatch.description:
The Docs search stage defaults. Every field is optional so the Docs tab can
move one knob without restating the rest.

content_hash.description: Gates incremental re-ingest: unchanged pages never re-run the model.

job_id.description:
Id of the `hf_download` job currently transferring this file, if any —
what "Cancel" acts on. `None` means nothing is running for this row.

requested_revision.description:
The revision the download asks for: `main`, or the commit an audio
catalog entry pins. `None` on a row from before it was recorded (a
`main` download).

resolved_commit.description:
The commit the file on disk came from (the hub's `X-Repo-Commit`).
`None` when unknown — every row downloaded before it was recorded.

status.description:
`queued | downloading | done | failed | update_available` — a row that
claims queued/downloading with no live progress is *interrupted*
(derived, never stored).

DownloadedFrom.description: Where a downloaded weights file came from.

DraftStats.description:
Speculative decoding's draft statistics, summed over a point's requests. Present only when the
server reported them.

EditApplied.description:
One Dockerfile edit's result in a resolved preview: the run log's
"applied (N matches)" / "not matched", as data.

applied.description:
Occurrences replaced; `0` = not matched (a run fails on that when the
edit is `required`).

index.description: Position in the edit list, from 0 (an edit's `name` may be empty).

EditRole.description:
What a Dockerfile edit is for. The role is what lets the build's
own switches reach an edit that was customized: `ccache` off drops every
`ccache` and `cache` edit, whether it came
from the preset or was typed by hand.

oneOf.description:
Compiler-cache wiring: the `ccache` package, the cache mount, the
compiler launchers, the stats line.

Another build cache mount (the web UI's npm cache). Optional, and a
cache like ccache: off with it.

Build number / commit / date injection, so `--version` names what was
built even though `.git` is not in the build context.

`docker.io/` in front of a bare base image, so it resolves without a
short-name alias.
A different base-image variant (sd.cpp's `-cudnn-` dropped).
Anything else — what a hand-written edit is unless it says otherwise.

dimensions.description: Forwarded (Gemini: outputDimensionality). A route that answers with another length — llama-server has no such parameter — is refused with 400 rather than served full-length vectors.

encoding_format.description: Encoded by the gateway, whatever the upstream: base64 is the little-endian float32 bytes, as OpenAI serves it.

input.description: A string, or an array of strings. Token-id arrays are refused with 400: an alias can route to a model with another tokenizer.

embedding.description: Floats, or a base64 string when encoding_format was base64.

Energy.description: The energy of a measured window: a point's, summed over its repetitions.

joules.description: The whole card, idle draw included.

seconds.description: Length of the measured windows, summed.

tokens.description:
The tokens those windows produced (prefill: prompt tokens; decode:
generated tokens).

tokens_per_joule.description: `tokens / joules`; `None` when the windows measured 0 J.

tokens_per_joule_each.description:
Tokens per joule of each window on its own (one per repetition, or
per request for prefill): the spread the comparison reads as this
figure's noise. A half-second decode window right after an idle
moment is measured while the card's clocks ramp up — live, decode at
depth 64 read 2.47 and 3.01 tok/J in two runs of identical settings.
Windows the counter did not move over are left out.

EnergySource.description: Where a joule figure came from.

oneOf.description:
The driver's total-energy counter, read at both ends of the window
(NVML `nvmlDeviceGetTotalEnergyConsumption`).

Power samples integrated over the window (trapezoids), because the
counter is not available.

EnergySummary.description: The run's VRAM and energy picture.

baseline_vram_bytes.description: Device VRAM used before the bench container started.

idle_power_w.description: Mean power over the baseline window, so a view can show net energy.

source.description:
How the run's joules were measured; `None` when the GPU reports no
power at all (then `unavailable` says why).

Engine.description:
Which of the three engines lmgw runs a build produces. ik_llama.cpp is
`Llama` with its own repo preset, not an engine of its own: its images run
in the same classes.

oneOf.description: llama.cpp and ik_llama.cpp — `llama-server`.
audio.cpp — `audiocpp_server`.
stable-diffusion.cpp — `sd-server`.

refusal.description:
True when this kind is lmgw refusing, rather than an upstream or a
client failing — the two belong in different colours.

EvalRunRow.description:
One measured run. `params` is the stage parameter set it was measured under —
two runs under different parameters are not comparable, so the numbers
never travel without them.

orphaned_queries.description:
Queries whose every expected chunk is gone — they score zero for a
reason that is not "retrieval got worse".

Example.description:
One static example exchange: what the user says, and how the model
replies. Both sides are non-empty.

ExportAttachment.description: An attachment as the export carries it: its metadata, position and bytes.

blockers.description: For a draft: why it cannot be sent to the thread's current model.

data.description: The file's bytes, base64 (standard alphabet, padded).

extracted.description:
The text extracted from it (a PDF's pages, an office file, an audio
file's transcript); `null` when there is none.

extracted_tokens.description: The extracted text's token estimate; `null` when there is none.

hints.description:
For a draft: what it becomes on the way, sent all the same (an image
as a placeholder, a PDF's pages as its text) under a fallback that
cannot see.

kind.description: `image`, `pdf`, `text`, `audio`, ... as the upload was classified.

meta.description:
What extraction found: pages, text-less pages, class, sheets,
transcript alias or error, tokens. `{}` for an image.

mode.description:
A text-class PDF's choice, `text` or `images`; `null` when it does
not apply or is not chosen yet.

ord.description: Its position among its message's files.

ExportMessage.description:
A message as the export carries it: the columns of a stored message with
its `ir_messages` parsed, and the files sent with it.

ir_messages.description:
An agentic turn's tool calls and results as the JSON value the
record holds; `null` for a plain turn. When the record does not
parse, its raw text and `ir_messages_unparsed: true`.

ir_messages_unparsed.description:
Set (to `true`) only when `ir_messages` is the raw text of a record
that did not parse.

ExportRef.description: A folder or personality profile named in an export.

ExportThread.description:
A thread as the export carries it: the columns of the thread list's row
(`ThreadRow`) except the two derived from other rows, `last_message_at`
and `purge_at`.

kind.description: `chat` or `admin`.

temporary.description: The thread was held in memory only (a temporary chat).

ExtraChange.description: One unpinned extra's change since the last verified run.

change.description:
The badge's own wording: `"pushed"`, `"closed unmerged"`, or one
of the two "merged upstream" readings (see `reasons` of the update status).

FeedHold.description:
The GPU hold: whether local models are paused, and the alias that answers
for them meanwhile. The `hold` event and part of
[`Hello`].

FeedPrincipal.description:
Who the feed is for: its kind and the name it is known by, without the
kind's prefix. A paired device is kind `device`, named as it was paired
("desktop", not "device:desktop"); the gateway's administrator has the
other kind: the dashboard (named `dashboard`) or an admin key (named as
the key without its prefix).

Folder.description:
A Chat folder as `GET /chat/api/folders` lists it, with its thread
counts as the caller may see them.

archive_days.description:
Days without activity before one of its threads is archived; `null`
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. Set from the dashboard: a device
key cannot change it.

devices_hidden.description:
Set when a device deleted this folder while it held threads that
device could not see: the folder stays for them, hidden from every
device, until it is shown to devices again from the dashboard. Always
`false` for a device key, which never sees such a folder.

name.description: Folder names need not be unique.

ongoing.description: `null` for a folder that is not one ongoing conversation.

purge_days.description:
Days after archiving before one of its threads is deleted; `null`
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. Set from the dashboard: a device
key cannot change it.

sort.description: The folder's place in the list.

FolderChanged.description:
`folder.created` / `folder.updated` for a folder that exists at
delivery: the folder as `GET /chat/api/folders` lists it now (its counts
as the reader may see them), with `by` beside its fields.

archive_days.description:
Days without activity before one of its threads is archived; `null`
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. Set from the dashboard: a device
key cannot change it.

by.description: Who made the change; `null` for the gateway's own.

devices_hidden.description:
Set when a device deleted this folder while it held threads that
device could not see: the folder stays for them, hidden from every
device, until it is shown to devices again from the dashboard. Always
`false` for a device key, which never sees such a folder.

name.description: Folder names need not be unique.

ongoing.description: `null` for a folder that is not one ongoing conversation.

purge_days.description:
Days after archiving before one of its threads is deleted; `null`
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. Set from the dashboard: a device
key cannot change it.

sort.description: The folder's place in the list.

FolderGone.description:
`folder.deleted`, and `folder.created` / `folder.updated` for a folder
that is gone by the time the event is delivered.

FolderOngoing.description:
The `ongoing` field of a folder: `null` for a folder that is not an
ongoing conversation.

current_thread_id.description:
The thread the conversation continues in; `null` until the first
`current` call, after its thread was deleted, moved out of the
folder or archived by hand, and, for a device key, while the thread
is out of the key's reach.

idle_minutes.description:
Minutes without a message after which the next `current` call starts
a new thread. `0`: a new thread only when a client asks for one.

FolderRef.description: A folder named by its id and name.

Forge.description: Where a build's repository lives, which decides how PR extras are found.

oneOf.description: PRs are `refs/pull/<n>/head`, details from the GitHub REST API.
MRs are `refs/merge-requests/<n>/head`, details from `/api/v4`.
No PR list and no forge API: refs from other remotes only.

ForgePr.description: One PR (GitHub) or MR (GitLab) as the extras picker shows it.

merge_commit_sha.description:
The commit the merge put on its target branch — the merge, squash or
rebase commit (GitHub `merge_commit_sha`; GitLab `merge_commit_sha`,
else `squash_commit_sha`). Empty when the forge gives none (an open
PR, an old GitLab). A build skips a merged PR as "merged upstream"
only when its base contains this commit (or the PR's head).

merged_at.description: Set once the forge reports it merged.

FtsWeightsPatch.description: The four BM25 column weights, each optional like every other stage default.

FtsWeightsView.description: BM25 column weights, in `chunk_fts` column order.

path.description: Relative to models_dir — exactly what the path fields take.

GoldenCandidateRow.description:
One generated query awaiting a decision. It is **not** a golden query: an
eval never scores it, and only an accept turns it into one.

decided_at.description: Empty while it is still pending.

expected_chunk_ids.description:
The chunk it was written from — attached by code, never named by the
model.

golden_query_id.description: The golden query it became, when it was accepted.

model.description: The model that wrote it — the corpus's pinned ingest model.

rationale.description: The model's sentence about why that chunk answers it.

GpuBackend.description:
The GPU backend a build targets. Labelled **GPU backend** on the
Backends page, so it does not read as the page's own subject. Picks the
preset's Dockerfile candidate.

GpuIdentity.description:
The GPU the run used, as far as the sampler sees it. Sums and maxima over the visible
devices.

clock_events.description: The OR of every sample's clock-event reasons.

name.description: The first device's name (a comparison key).

telemetry.description: The GPU probe's own label (`NVML (driver …)`, or why there is none).

throttled.description:
Whether any of those is a throttling reason: NVML's software power cap
(`0x4`), hardware slowdown (`0x8`), software or hardware thermal
slowdown (`0x20`, `0x40`) or power-brake slowdown (`0x80`). Idle, the
applications-clocks setting, sync boost and the display clock are
states, not throttling. A run that throttled reports the throttled
numbers.

GroupApplied.description:
A group, `apply`: every running member recreated, and the static checks
over every enabled model in scope.

held.description: Stopped and not started again because the GPU hold is on.

Left running untouched because the GPU hold would not let them start
again.

GroupStarted.description: A group, `start`: only the models flagged warm_start are started.

held.description: Left alone because the GPU hold is on.

vram.description: The GPU ledger, whole even when one group was asked about.

busy.description: Still serving requests and left running; `override` forces them.

Headline.description:
The headline numbers of one run, each `None` when the run did not
measure it.

decode_deep_tok_s.description: Decode tok/s at the deepest point, *D_max*.

decode_tokens_per_joule.description: Decode tokens per joule at depth 64.

load_vram_bytes.description: VRAM the load took (after load minus the baseline).

prefill_tok_s.description: Prefill tok/s at 2048 tokens, or the nearest measured length.

prefill_tokens.description: The length it was measured at.

HoldFallbackMode.description:
Per-model override of the GPU hold's fallback lookup: whether a held
request against this row falls back to the global chat alias, refuses
outright, or names its own alias.

oneOf.description:
Chat: fall through to `settings.hold.fallback_alias`. Aux/audio: no
fallback — they never inherit the global (a different embedding
model silently corrupts a vector index).

Refuse a held request against this row even if a global fallback is
configured.
Use this row's own `hold_fallback` alias.

HoldSettingsDto.description:
The GPU hold settings. `active` is
reported here but never settable through `SettingsFullPatch` — it is
toggled only through the `hold_set` op, because engaging it has the side
effect of stopping containers.

HoldSettingsPatch.description:
The GPU hold's global fallback. Carries no `active` field: engaging the
hold runs the GPU sweep, a side effect a generic settings patch must not
have, so the switch itself is flipped only through the `hold_set`
operation. A patch that names `active` is rejected, like any other field
this route does not carry.

fallback_alias.description:
`""` clears it back to "refuse"; otherwise validated (must resolve,
must not be local) before it is stored.

logical_cpus.description: Online logical CPUs, SMT siblings included.

physical_cores.description:
Physical cores, or the logical count when the topology is unreadable
(`source`).

source.description:
`topology` (counted from the kernel's CPU topology) | `logical` (the
topology could not be read, so the logical count stands in).

HostSettings.description:
Settings → MCP (`mcp.*` in `GET /api/settings-full`): the host link's
limits, each explicit on the link's WebSocket (§5.1), and the MCP Tasks
poll interval.

host_max_frame_mb.description: The largest frame, in MiB; `0` = bounded by `host_max_message_mb`.

host_max_message_mb.description:
The largest message a device may send, in MiB; `0` = no bound of its
own (a frame is then bounded by `host_max_frame_mb`). Not `0`
together with `host_max_frame_mb`. A full-desktop screenshot is the
expected large message.

host_ping_interval_s.description:
Seconds between the link's pings; a ping with no pong for a whole
interval closes the link. `0` = no pings, and no bound on a device
that stopped answering.

task_poll_interval_s.description:
Seconds between two `tasks/get` of an MCP task whose server suggests
no `pollInterval` of its own (MCP Tasks design §5.2); a server's
status notifications act at once. At least `1`.

ImageCapabilities.description:
One sd-server's own answer about the pipeline it loaded.

Every field defaults, because this is the one payload in the class that
comes from a moving container tag: a build that stops reporting a number
must leave the rest readable rather than fail the frame.

supported_modes.description:
`["img_gen"]`, `["img_gen","vid_gen"]` — what the loaded pipeline can
actually do, as opposed to what the row claims.

ImageEditField.description: One text field of an edit, as sent.

ImageEditFile.description: One file part of an edit, as sent.

name.description: `image` or `mask`.

type.description:
The part's content type as the upload declared it; `null` if it
declared none.

ImageEditSummary.description:
What an edit sent, in place of a JSON body: its text fields and each file
by name and size.

ImageEditsRequest.description: Refused unless the resolved model's row has its edit pipeline enabled.

image.description: One or more image files. lmgw relays every multipart field named image verbatim, with no cardinality check of its own.

ImageFeatures.description:
Which optional inputs the loaded pipeline admits to accepting. Not an edit
gate — the row's `edit` column is.

ImageGenForm.description:
Everything the lab's two panels collect, as typed. Numbers travel as the
strings the inputs hold: an empty field means "say nothing about this", not
zero, and a malformed one has to be reportable as a message rather than
silently become a default.

model.description:
The public alias — `image/<id>` for a local row, the alias for a cloud
one. Rewritten to the concrete upstream id by the route itself.

seed.description:
Blank says nothing (sd-server's own default is a fixed 42); `-1` is its
spelling for "random each run".

ImageGenerationsRequest.description: Other keys are forwarded for a cloud image upstream.

prompt.description: May carry a trailing <sd_cpp_extra_args>{…}</sd_cpp_extra_args> block of raw sd.cpp CLI arguments; the dashboard's Image lab builds this block and is the reference for its contents.

ImageGenerationsResponse.description: The upstream's answer, relayed as it sends it: each image carries what response_format asked for, plus whatever else the upstream adds (revised_prompt).

items.description: One image: b64_json, or url when the request asked for response_format url (an upstream's default, dall-e's, for instance).

ImageLabEditRequest.description: multipart/form-data. The body size is not limited.

form.description: The form as a JSON string: an ImageGenForm, the same document the generate route takes as its body.

image.description: The picture to edit.

ImageLabModel.description:
One model the Image lab can generate with: a local `image/<id>` row, or a
cloud alias whose upstream catalog says it draws. `C` is the shape of the
probed capabilities: the gateway fills in its own, a reader (and the API
document) uses [`ImageCapabilities`](crate::status::ImageCapabilities).

args.description:
The flags a local row's container is started with (`width`, `height`,
`steps`, `cfg_scale`, `sampling_method` are the form's defaults when
set); `null` for a cloud alias.

image_capabilities.description:
What the running container reported about its loaded pipeline: the
samplers, schedulers, size bounds and LoRAs on disk. `null` until a
container has been probed.

local.description: A local row of this gateway, not a cloud alias.

model_id.description: The local row's model id; `null` for a cloud alias.

modes.description:
A local row's pipelines (`img_gen`, `vid_gen`, ...), as the operator
declared them; `null` for a cloud alias.

name.description: The alias to send as `model`.

notes.description: What the gateway noticed about the model, one sentence each.

owner.description: The upstream that serves it (`local` for the gateway's own rows).

state.description:
A local row's container state (`starting`, `ready`, `stopping`);
`null` when it has none running, and for a cloud alias.

task.description: The model's task, as `GET /v1/models` reports it.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems the running container's start found.

ImageLoraRow.description:
One row of the optional LoRA table. `<lora:…>` prompt tags are refused by
every sd.cpp family, so a LoRA is this structured field or nothing.

multiplier.description: Blank leaves the server's own multiplier in place.

path.description:
A name from the probed `loras` list, or a path the server can resolve
under its `--lora-model-dir`.

ImageModel.description:
An image model row — one stable-diffusion.cpp pipeline.

The two JSON-map fields stay dynamic on purpose, exactly as the server
types them: sd.cpp adds a model family and its flag every few weeks, and
the keys are validated against the container image's own `--help` rather
than against any enum on either side of this wire.

args.description:
Runtime + default-generation flags, same key convention. A `true`
renders as a bare switch.

capabilities_override.description: An alias's capabilities override for the derived `/v1/models` capability facts.

edit.description: The pipeline takes reference images and may serve `/v1/images/edits`.

extra_run_args.description: Per-model `podman run` args override; `None` inherits the class's.

files.description:
Flag key → path relative to the image models dir. Exactly one of
`model` / `diffusion_model` is present on a valid row.

hold_fallback_mode.description:
`inherit` | `none` | `alias`. `inherit` means "no fallback" for this
class — an image row never inherits the global chat alias.

idle_seconds.description: Seconds idle before the container is stopped; `0` never reaps.

image.description:
Per-model container image override; `None` inherits the image class
settings' image.

peak_extra_bytes.description:
The learned transient peak: what one generation was measured to need
above this pipeline's idle residency. Written by
the gateway, not by the editor — a `files` or `args` change resets it
to `None`, because a different pipeline has a different peak.

peak_learned_at.description: When that figure was observed; `None` whenever the peak is.

extra_run_args.description: `podman run` args override, one per line; null inherits.

files.description: Flag key to path under the image models dir.

files_present.description: For each key of `files`, whether the file (or directory) exists.

peak_extra_bytes.description:
Bytes one generation was measured to need above idle residency;
null until one has run.

public_name.description: The name clients call it by, with the image prefix.

ImageProvenance.description:
An image's build provenance: read
from the `dev.lmgw.*` OCI labels, so an image stays self-describing even
